\par\smallskip
{\small \textbf{S1} The rewrite. Describe the economy, define its equilibrium and characterize it, then derive the results, solve the example, and end with the evidence and the history.\par \textbf{S2} The original's order. The demand side and the cost system come first, then the outside option, then the labor market where the two meet; the rewrite's formal content is placed in these sections.\par \textbf{S3} Facts first. The three measured facts come right after the introduction, so the reader meets the fork, the coverage ratio and the financing gap before the model that accounts for them.\par \textbf{S4} Sections named for questions. After the model, each section answers one question the paper asks, and its title is that question.\par \textbf{S5} The two chains. The paper follows the two chains of the introduction: the demand side and replacement, then the supply side and the outside option, then the labor market where they meet.\par \textbf{S6} From simple to general. The model is built up in steps: an economy small enough to solve by hand, the four-good economy, its numerical instance, and general production networks, before the results that use them.\par \textbf{S7} Literature and history first. Earlier accounts of the wage and the history of work come before the model as its motivation; the model, results and evidence follow.\par \textbf{S8} Policy at the center. The fiscal side becomes a main section: the rent tax, coverage and the transition from Appendix D, after the measurement that supplies their numbers.}\par

options.label: The rewrite
options.tex:
\emph{Describe the economy, define its equilibrium and characterize it, then derive the results, solve the example, and end with the evidence and the history.}\par\smallskip
\textbf{1\enspace Introduction} (2.3 pp.)\par\nopagebreak{\small The history opening, the two questions and chains, the claim, the roadmap.}\par
\textbf{2\enspace Description of the economy} (1 pp.)\par\nopagebreak{\small The economy in words, after Lucas (1978).}\par
\textbf{3\enspace Definition of equilibrium} (7.2 pp.)\par\nopagebreak{\small Assumptions 1-5, the cost system, government, Definitions 1-3; Table 1.}\par
\textbf{4\enspace Equilibrium} (5.6 pp.)\par\nopagebreak{\small Prices and the task margin, replacement closure, participation, existence and uniqueness.}\par
\textbf{5\enspace Purchasing power and income} (3.5 pp.)\par\nopagebreak{\small The real-wage fork, vanishing purchasing power, factor income.}\par
\textbf{6\enspace Distribution: rent taxation and a uniform transfer} (2.2 pp.)\par\nopagebreak{\small Proposition 6, coverage, fiscal capacity as wage income vanishes.}\par
\textbf{7\enspace A numerical economy and an automation path} (2.4 pp.)\par\nopagebreak{\small The calibrated instance, both channels, the path to low participation.}\par
\textbf{8\enspace Measurement} (2.3 pp.)\par\nopagebreak{\small The fork, coverage, financing against production.}\par
\textbf{9\enspace History and stabilizers} (3.2 pp.)\par\nopagebreak{\small Four configurations of the schedule; possible stabilizers.}\par
\textbf{10\enspace Artificial intelligence and conclusion} (1.6 pp.)\par\nopagebreak{\small AI in the two channels, the conjecture, future work.}\par
\smallskip{\small\textbf{Appendices.} A, proofs. B, extensions: production networks, several non-produced inputs, machine types and trade, worker types, ideas and institutional rents, task-level costs. C, expenditure shares under substitution. D, fiscal transition while labor remains employed. E, human-required tasks. F, the financing and production accounts.}\par
{\small\textbf{New content.} None.}\par
{\small\textbf{Main text.} about 31 pages.}

options.label: The original's order
options.tex:
\emph{The demand side and the cost system come first, then the outside option, then the labor market where the two meet; the rewrite's formal content is placed in these sections.}\par\smallskip
\textbf{1\enspace Introduction} (2.3 pp.)\par\nopagebreak{\small The rewrite's history opening ahead of main.tex's introduction, with its summary of results; the pointer to the old Section 2 becomes a roadmap.}\par
\textbf{2\enspace The model: task assignment and the cost system} (8.8 pp.)\par\nopagebreak{\small The economy in words, tasks and the margin, the cost recursion, closing the replacement price, two margins of automation.}\par
\textbf{3\enspace The outside option: pricing exit} (2.2 pp.)\par\nopagebreak{\small The basket, workers, the owner and support, Proposition 3.}\par
\textbf{4\enspace Replacement meets participation} (5.2 pp.)\par\nopagebreak{\small Government, the definition of equilibrium, labor-market clearing, Theorem 1, and the numerical economy (main.tex's Appendix B).}\par
\textbf{5\enspace Purchasing power at an interior margin} (3.5 pp.)\par\nopagebreak{\small What an hour's wage buys; factor income while labor remains employed.}\par
\textbf{6\enspace Distribution: rent taxation and a uniform transfer} (2.2 pp.)\par\nopagebreak{\small As in the rewrite's Section 6.}\par
\textbf{7\enspace History as four configurations of the model} (2.6 pp.)\par\nopagebreak{\small The four configurations, before the measurements.}\par
\textbf{8\enspace Measurement} (2.3 pp.)\par\nopagebreak{\small The fork, coverage, financing against production.}\par
\textbf{9\enspace Possible stabilizers} (0.6 pp.)\par\nopagebreak{\small As in the original.}\par
\textbf{10\enspace Artificial intelligence and conclusion} (0.9 pp.)\par\nopagebreak{\small As in the rewrite, without the future work.}\par
\textbf{11\enspace Future work} (0.7 pp.)\par\nopagebreak{\small A section of its own, as in the original.}\par
\smallskip{\small\textbf{Appendices.} A, proofs, task-level costs, timing and institutional rents (main.tex A.2-A.4; A.1's environment is now in Sections 2-4). B, extensions as in the rewrite (main.tex B's numerical economy is now in Section 4). C, factor income and expenditure shares. D, fiscal transition. E, human-required tasks. F, the financing and production accounts.}\par
{\small\textbf{New content.} None. The roadmap and some section openings are rewritten for the order.}\par
{\small\textbf{Main text.} about 31 pages.}

options.label: Sections named for questions
options.tex:
\emph{After the model, each section answers one question the paper asks, and its title is that question.}\par\smallskip
\textbf{1\enspace Introduction} (2.8 pp.)\par\nopagebreak{\small As in the rewrite, with a numbered list of contributions (new).}\par

options.label: The two chains
options.tex:
\emph{The paper follows the two chains of the introduction: the demand side and replacement, then the supply side and the outside option, then the labor market where they meet.}\par\smallskip
\textbf{1\enspace Introduction} (2.8 pp.)\par\nopagebreak{\small As in the rewrite, with a figure of the two chains (new).}\par
\textbf{2\enspace The economy and its cost system} (5 pp.)\par\nopagebreak{\small The description, the technology assumptions, the cost system that both chains use.}\par
\textbf{3\enspace The demand side: replacement} (3.8 pp.)\par\nopagebreak{\small The two channels, the task margin, replacement closure; results stated at prices that satisfy the cost system.}\par
\textbf{4\enspace The supply side: the outside option} (4.7 pp.)\par\nopagebreak{\small Workers, the owner and support, participation, and what an hour's wage buys against the basket.}\par
\textbf{5\enspace Where the two sides meet} (4.9 pp.)\par\nopagebreak{\small The definition of equilibrium, labor-market clearing, Theorem 1, the numerical economy.}\par
\textbf{6\enspace Who pays for support} (3.5 pp.)\par\nopagebreak{\small Government instruments, factor income, the rent tax and transfer, fiscal capacity.}\par
\textbf{7\enspace Evidence: measurement and history} (4.9 pp.)\par\nopagebreak{\small The measured fork, coverage and financing, then the four configurations.}\par
\textbf{8\enspace Stabilizers, artificial intelligence and conclusion} (2.2 pp.)\par\nopagebreak{\small Possible stabilizers, AI, future work.}\par
\smallskip{\small\textbf{Appendices.} A, proofs. B, extensions: production networks, several non-produced inputs, machine types and trade, worker types, ideas and institutional rents, task-level costs. C, expenditure shares under substitution. D, fiscal transition while labor remains employed. E, human-required tasks. F, the financing and production accounts.}\par
{\small\textbf{New content.} A figure of the two chains in the introduction (new, half a page). Short openings that place each section on its chain (new).}\par
{\small\textbf{Main text.} about 32 pages.}
